newsitem.title: USA: NY Senate head sees passage of energy tax cut bill.
newsitem.headline: NY Senate head sees passage of energy tax cut bill.

text.p: New York Senate Leader Joseph Bruno today said the Senate will pass a bill which would cut state energy tax and save state ratepayers $710 million by the year 2001.
The bill calls for phase-out of the Gross Receipts Tax (GRT) on energy. It would freeze GRT in 1997, then phase it out over the next four years.
"When New Yorkers pay their utility bills, an average of 18 cents out of every dollar goes to pay state and local taxes," said Bruno in a statement.

"That's the highest energy tax burden in the nation and double the national average. Getting rid of the Gross Receipts Tax will bring rates down and provide the most direct savings to consumers," he added.
"The Gross Receipts Tax artificially inflates prices. It's an appropriate tax to repeal," said Assemblyman Paul Tonko, chairman of the state assembly's energy committee.

An assembly version of a GRT repeal was introduced on March 4. The measure still needs to be reviewed and passed by the assembly energy and ways and means committees before it could be voted on by the entire assembly.
The GRT proposal is one of three energy bills to be taken up Wednesday by the state senate.

The "Electric Ratepayer Relief Act" submitted by Gov George Pataki would establish a financing mechanism for the state's electric utilities to obtain lower cost financing which will result in lower electric rates.
The Senate has passed this bill twice. However, the bill has yet to be introduced by the state assembly majority, Bruno noted.

The last proposal would make 400 megawatts (MW) of low cost power available for economic development. This low-cost power would be provided jointly by the New York Power Authority and investor-owned utilities.
The low-cost energy would be made available to businesses for the purpose of job retention.
